title: Fallback path skips _validate_user_contract, so a drifted contract= annotation is not caught at parse time
description: The healthy parser resolves config through _resolve_node_config, which calls _validate_user_contract to cross-check a `contract=` kwarg against the builder-derived contract and raises ContractMismatchError on disagreement (_config_builder.py:434). fallback_parse builds config directly via _build_node_config and merely re-attaches `config['contract'] = decorator_kwargs['contract']` (lines 740-741) with no validation. Contract validation is config-only (it does not require the file to be syntactically whole), so a wrong/drifted contract annotation in a broken file silently survives parse-time. The mismatch is only re-detected later at execution time, diverging from the project's fail-loud-at-parse philosophy that the healthy path implements.
evidence: _resolve_node_config:434 `_validate_user_contract(node_type, config, user_contract, func_name)` raises ContractMismatchError (_config_builder.py:364-372). fallback_parse never calls _resolve_node_config or _validate_user_contract; it only does the unconditional re-attach at 740-741. Compare _config_builder.py:441-442 which attaches AFTER validation.
